prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Stored/reloaded OAuth tokens don't get their expiry timestamp reconstructed at provider initialization, so is_token_valid() treats a stale token as valid indefinitely and the proactive silent-refresh path never fires after a process restart. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #1784 fixes the root cause directly in `_initialize()` by computing `token_expiry_time` from the stored token's `expires_in` right when tokens are loaded, is a 4-line change, and ships a dedicated `expired_tokens` regression fixture. #2875's own inline comment states the identical root cause ('A provider reloaded from storage never restores token_expiry_time, so is_token_valid() treats the stale token as valid and the proactive-refresh branch above is skipped') but instead works around it by adding a new 'Step 3.5' refresh-before-reauth branch inside `async_auth_flow`'s 401 handler. prs.title: fix: buffer stdio server writes during progress notifications
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both modify the same anyio.create_memory_object_stream() calls in stdio_server() that set the read/write stream buffer sizes, and both trace back to the same root cause: a buffer size of 0 forces the write stream to rendezvous synchronously, which can block a handler that needs to enqueue a final response while an earlier message (e.g. a progress notification) is still being flushed to stdout. prs.cluster_pick_reason: #2654 fixes the blocking scenario by default (write buffer size changed from 0 to 1), so every existing caller of stdio_server() gets the fix automatically with no code changes on their end. Its diff also adds a new test (BlockingStdout) that reproduces the actual notification-vs-response ordering bug being fixed. #2215 only adds new read_stream_buffer_size/write_stream_buffer_size parameters that both default to 0 (i.e., unchanged current behavior), so it does not resolve the blocking issue unless a caller explicitly opts in by passing a non-default value, and its diff doesn't include a test demonstrating the bug scenario. Both PRs touch the exact same two lines that construct the memory object streams, so they will conflict if both are merged; #2654's default-value fix is the one that actually resolves the reported problem.

prs.title: fix(server): reject concurrent duplicate JSON-RPC request ids
prs.author: arimu1
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Concurrent/duplicate JSON-RPC request ids in StreamableHTTP's _handle_post_request can overwrite an in-flight entry in _request_streams, cross-wiring responses between two requests (one gets the other's payload, the other hangs). (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Concurrent/duplicate JSON-RPC request ids in StreamableHTTP's _handle_post_request can overwrite an in-flight entry in _request_streams, cross-wiring responses between two requests (one gets the other's payload, the other hangs). (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both PRs add the same in-flight-duplicate-id rejection, but #3063 keys _request_streams with str(message.id), which collapses distinct JSON-RPC ids (integer 1 and string "1" become the same key) and can still collide with the reserved GET_STREAM_KEY ("_GET_stream") if a client sends that exact string id — reintroducing the cross-wiring bug it's meant to fix, just for a narrower set of inputs. #3221 replaces this with a type-preserving _request_stream_key() helper ("i:" / "s:" prefixes) that keeps int/string ids distinct and can never equal GET_STREAM_KEY, closing both gaps while implementing the identical duplicate-id-rejection behavior.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs rewrite the same RequestResponder.cancel() logic to stop the spec-violating error-response-on-cancel behavior, but #2514 goes further: it covers request-timeout and caller-initiated cancellation (not just client-sent CancelledNotification) by emitting a proper notifications/cancelled message via the newly imported CancelledNotificationParams, and its diff removes the `# pragma: no cover` marker on the affected branch, indicating it adds test coverage for this path that #2493's diff does not show. #2493's server.py change only adjusts logging/comments around an already-duplicate-response check and its session.py fix is a strict subset of what #2514 delivers, so merging #2514 alone yields a superset fix.

members.title: fix: don't send a response for cancelled requests
members.author: Zelys-DFKH
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2514: RequestResponder.cancel() violates the MCP spec's cancellation semantics: on cancellation it used to send an error response to the client, but the spec requires receivers not send any response for a cancelled request. #2493 fixes this only for the case where the client itself sent a CancelledNotification (checks `message.cancelled` in server.py's _handle_request and drops the error-response code in session.py's cancel()). #2514 addresses the same root cancel() code path but more broadly: it imports CancelledNotificationParams and sends a proper `notifications/cancelled` message to the client, covering not just client-initiated cancellation but also server-side triggers (request timeout and caller-initiated cancellation) that #2493 leaves silent. Both PRs edit the same `cancel()` method in src/mcp/shared/session.py and are alternate fixes for the same underlying 'improper response on cancel' bug.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs add the same in-flight-duplicate-id rejection, but #3063 keys _request_streams with str(message.id), which collapses distinct JSON-RPC ids (integer 1 and string "1" become the same key) and can still collide with the reserved GET_STREAM_KEY ("_GET_stream") if a client sends that exact string id — reintroducing the cross-wiring bug it's meant to fix, just for a narrower set of inputs. #3221 replaces this with a type-preserving _request_stream_key() helper ("i:" / "s:" prefixes) that keeps int/string ids distinct and can never equal GET_STREAM_KEY, closing both gaps while implementing the identical duplicate-id-rejection behavior.
